canonical_title: Philip K. Dick Reviews Herman Wouk's The Caine Mutiny
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A short 1955 book review attributed to Dick, dated October 3, 1955, and preserved as a single scanned page, an early trace of his critical prose well before his major fiction.
page_summary:
This one-page item preserves an early book review, dated October 3, 1955, in which Dick appraises Herman Wouk's bestselling naval novel The Caine Mutiny. It dates from the period when Dick was publishing short stories in the science-fiction magazines and had not yet written the novels that would define his reputation.

As a scanned single page, the document's value is largely biographical and archival: it shows Dick engaging with mainstream literary fiction and working in a critical register rather than a fictional one. It offers a small window onto his tastes and judgments at the outset of his career.

The portal holds one archive manifestation. Given the brevity of the source, the entry is best treated as a documentary artifact rather than a major statement.
